title: NightEagle Expands Into Russia With GhostContainer Backdoor and RDP Tunneling Tools
content_md: NightEagle, also tracked as APT-Q-95, has expanded its targeting to Russian businesses after previously focusing mainly on organizations across Asia. The threat group has been active since at least 2023 and is now using compromised VPN credentials, Microsoft Exchange backdoors, RDP tunneling tools , and Active Directory attack techniques to gain and maintain access. Investigations by Kaspersky’s Global Emergency Response Team found that NightEagle combines legitimate tools with public offensive-security utilities. This approach helps the attackers blend into normal network activity while moving through victim environments. NightEagle Targets Russia Networks In most observed incidents, NightEagle gained initial access with valid but compromised corporate VPN credentials. The VPN sessions came from Russian IP addresses associated with Cloudflare WARP tunnels and from European virtual private server infrastructure. After accessing the network, the group deployed the GhostContainer backdoor on Microsoft Exchange servers. GhostContainer samples identified by the Similarity technology from Kaspersky Threat Analysis (Source: securelist) GhostContainer is a .NET-based malware that contains elements from publicly available projects, including Neo-reGeorg, a CVE-2020-0688 exploit, and the GhostWebShell component from ysoserial.
